categories.label: Verification coverage
categories.evaluate: Unit, integration, API, UI, or end-to-end tests exist where appropriate; tests cover important behavior and are runnable locally with documented commands

categories.label: Build and delivery hygiene
categories.evaluate: Build, lint, typecheck, test, CI, and release/deploy workflows are discoverable, repeatable, and aligned with documented commands

categories.label: Runtime and dependency health
categories.evaluate: Language runtimes, frameworks, package managers, IaC tooling, providers, images, and core dependencies are supported, intentionally versioned, and not known EOL according to checked-in reference data

categories.label: Repository hygiene
categories.evaluate: The repo has expected stack files, lockfiles where appropriate, useful gitignore coverage, generated/cache/build outputs excluded, and safe example config without real secrets

categories.label: Credential and identity hygiene
categories.evaluate: Secrets are not committed; password, API-key, token, and client-secret use is isolated and documented; cloud or CI/CD integrations prefer managed identity, workload identity, OIDC, IAM roles, or secret-store references where supported

categories.label: Infrastructure as Code hygiene
categories.evaluate: When IaC or deployment configuration is present, infrastructure changes are repeatable, reviewable, validated, version-aware, and safely separated across environments

categories.label: Code organization
categories.evaluate: Module boundaries are clear; domain logic is separated from framework glue where practical; file layout is predictable; large files, tangled dependencies, and copy-paste duplication are limited

categories.label: Change safety
categories.evaluate: Common changes are localized; APIs, storage, migrations, config, and compatibility risks are handled deliberately; rollback or recovery paths exist for risky changes

categories.label: Operational support
categories.evaluate: Logs, errors, health checks, configuration, observability, and debugging instructions are useful enough to operate and troubleshoot the software

categories.label: Documentation and onboarding
categories.evaluate: README, setup, architecture, contribution, testing, deployment, and troubleshooting docs exist where useful and match actual files, scripts, and workflows

bands.label: Difficult
bands.interpretation: The repo is expensive and risky to change because verification, setup, ownership, or key maintenance signals are missing

bands.label: Basic
bands.interpretation: The repo has some maintainability foundations, but important checks or conventions are incomplete or person-dependent

bands.label: Serviceable
bands.interpretation: A competent developer can make normal changes with moderate confidence using repo-local commands, tests, and conventions

bands.label: Healthy
bands.interpretation: The repo supports safe routine change through clear structure, validation, dependency hygiene, and operational practices

bands.label: Durable
bands.interpretation: The repo is highly maintainable across teams, environments, and time, with strong automation, currency, and safety controls

caps.reason: No automated test files or test scripts found; docs-only validation can earn only partial verification credit
No CI or pipeline configuration found; local commands can earn partial delivery hygiene credit
No .gitignore found; generated, cache, local configuration, or secret files may be accidentally tracked
Committed secret-like values or tracked local secret files were detected
Cloud deployment evidence exists but no IaC or deployment configuration was found

bandConstraints.requirement: Durable repositories have meaningful automated verification for important behavior
Durable repositories use supported core runtimes and avoid known EOL versions according to checked-in reference data
Durable repositories have no committed secrets and use appropriate secret or identity controls for integrations
Healthy repositories expose repeatable build or validation commands
Healthy repositories validate IaC through plan, preview, lint, format, template, or schema checks when IaC is present
